in_hebrew.name: גונחילדה
in_hebrew.meaning: מלחמת הקרב הקדושה נשמתה של אלוהים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: גונחילדה הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו במלחמת הקרב הקדושה, נשמתה של אלוהים, ומשמעותו לוחמת רבת עוצמה עבור אלוהים, שילוב של 'גון' שפירושו מלחמה, ו'חילד' שפירושו ילדה או צעירה, ומדגיש את הדבקות וההקרבה לנושא הרוחני.

in_greek.name: Γκουνχίλδα
in_greek.long_meaning: Γκουνχίλδα προέρχεται από τους Γερμανικούς όρους 'gun' που σημαίνει πόλεμος και 'hild' που σημαίνει μάχη ή πολεμίστρια, αναφερόμενη στη δύναμη και το πάθος για το θείο, και συνδέεται με την πνευματική αγωνία και την αφοσίωση στο Χριστό.

in_latin.name: Gunhilda
in_latin.long_meaning: Gunhilda derivatur ex terminis Germanicis 'gun' quod significat bellum et 'hild' quod significat proelium vel bellatrix, referens ad fortitudinem et devotionem ad divina, et coniungitur cum spirituali certamine et dedicatione ad Christum.

In many tales and legends, Gunhilda is depicted as a defender of her people and a champion of justice.

historical_references.reference: Gunhilda was a Frankish princess, the daughter of Clovis II, King of the Franks and his wife Clotilde. She was born around 632 and died around 680. She is best known for her role in the early medieval legends of the Frankish princesses known as the Merowingian legend, which portrayed her as a powerful and independent woman who ruled her duchy with authority.

According to legend, Gunhilda was married to Thierry II, Duke of Austrasia, whom she is said to have ruled jointly with after his death. She is also said to have taken charge of her sons' education and ruled Austrasia as regent for them until they came of age. The legends portray Gunhilda as a powerful and wise ruler, who was respected by her subjects and feared by her enemies.
